subject: Error code when using a squared covariate in colext models

messages.author: 3c096b57b95a64c2
messages.subject: Error code when using a squared covariate in colext models
parts:
Hi All,

I'm trying to run multiseason occupancy models to assess the influence of altitude on the colonisation and extinction rates of multiple butterfly species in a Spanish mountain range, however I'm having trouble getting my models to run when using both altitude and altitude squared as my covariates.

Initially I was standardising my data for altitude to bring it closer to 0 (originally this variable ranged from ~800 to 2400), when standardising altitude my models were running fine, however I was advised that standardising this variable makes the coefficients uninterpretable.

I've attached a copy of the data that I'm using for one of the species (Hesperia comma) and below is my code:

library(unmarked)

data <- read.csv("Hcomma.csv")

y <- data[,3:12]

#Creating yearly site covariates

year <- as.character(c(2004,2017))

year<- matrix(year, nrow(data),2,byrow = TRUE)

year.covs <- data.frame(
  year = matrix(t(year),ncol = 1)
)

#Creating observational covariates

season    <- data[,15:24]


obs.cov   <-data.frame(season = matrix(t(season),ncol=1))

# Creating site covariates

site.cov <- data.frame(Alt = data[,13], AltSq = data[,14])

#Creating an unmarked frame

comma <- unmarkedMultFrame(
  y=y,
  yearlySiteCovs = year.covs,
  obsCovs = obs.cov,
  siteCovs = site.cov,
  numPrimary = 2
)

# fitting models

fm1<-colext( ~1,  ~1,  ~1, ~1, data=comma)

fm2<-colext( ~1, ~1, ~1, ~season, data=comma)

fm4<-colext( ~1, ~Alt, ~1, ~1, data=comma)

fm5<-colext( ~1, ~1, ~Alt, ~1, data=comma)

fm6<-colext( ~Alt, ~1, ~1, ~1, data=comma)

fm7 <-colext( ~Alt, ~Alt, ~Alt, ~1, data=comma) - These initial models above including just altitude run fine.

fm8<-colext( ~Alt+AltSq, ~Alt, ~Alt, ~1, data=comma) - However, as soon as I introduce AltSq, I get the following error code: 


> fm8<-colext( ~Alt+AltSq, ~Alt, ~Alt, ~1, data=comma)
Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = getHessian, ...) : 
  non-finite finite-difference value [3]


I've had a good read through examples online and threads on this group but can't seem to find an answer, I've tried specifying a 'starts' value, however this hasn't worked unfortunately.

Any help would be much appreciated, it may be something very simple, I'm very new to both R and Unmarked, my apologies!

Thanks very much,

Lee.

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Error code when using a squared covariate in colext models
parts:
"...however I was advised that standardising this variable makes the coefficients uninterpretable."  Nonsense for at least three reasons: (1) one can always transform back, (2) I think there are very few folks that can appropriately "interpret" coefficients on a logistic scale even when the original units are used, and (3) Squaring numbers in the thousands (or even the hundreds such as the year 2018) usually results in lots of round-off error which in turn produces error messages such as the one you see.

But one doesn't have to "standardize" by subtracting the mean and dividing by the standard deviation.  When one has elevation in feet or meters, dividing by 1,000 usually does the trick and makes it much easier to transform back.  (When one has the years 2003 through 2016, subtracting 2000 is probably all you need to do.)

 So changing the following lines of code from

# Creating site covariates 
site.cov <- data.frame(Alt = data[,13], AltSq = data[,14])

to
# Creating site covariates
site.cov <- data.frame(Alt = data[,13]/1000, AltSq = (data[,13]/1000)^2)

will remove the error messages.

But that results in getting lots of NaN's for the standard errors for the colonization and extinction parameter estimates which is a different issue.  (I'll look at that later today but that should NOT stop anyone else from looking into why that is happening.)

Jim

Dear Jim,

excellent remarks ! We transform covariates way too often in ways that makes interpretation of the coefficients really hard, e.g. by normalizing them. Instead, as you say, we should much better strive to transform them such that they keep some useful interpretation, e.g., that an altitude is expressed in kms instead of metres or a date in months instead of days etc.

Best regards  --- Marc

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Error code when using a squared covariate in colext models
parts:
So after dividing altitude by 1,000 and on some models adding in more iterations (control=list(maxit=10000)), the error messages should go away.  Some models involving altitude and altitude^2 will result in NaN's for the standard errors of the coefficients because altitude and altitude^2 are so highly correlated.

The squared term for altitude doesn't seem to add anything (both in terms of lower AIC and being statistically significant in the initial occupancy, colonization or extinction).  This might not be surprising because the range of altitude in the data still results in a correlation of 0.989 between altitude and altitude^2.  In other words, for this data set altitude and altitude^2 pretty much contribute the same information:


​

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Error code when using a squared covariate in colext models
parts:
To be clear, this is exactly why you should standardize (or center on the mean) before introducing a quadratic or interaction term. Doing so reduces the otherwise problematic multicollinearity.

Jim, if you plot standardized elevation vs. the square of standardized elevation, you’ll get a horseshoe shape with little correlation between the two. Otherwise the model has problems with fitting because the covariates are so highly correlated.

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Error code when using a squared covariate in colext models
parts:
Point well taken.

The predictions will be nearly identical either way - standardizing with centering or dividing by an appropriate constant (well, almost identical depending on round-off error, the relative tolerance setting, etc.) and I lean much more into selecting models based on the overall model fit rather than the statistical significance of the individual coefficients.

But looking at the parameter correlation matrix (cov2cor(m@opt$hessian) with m being the colext result), the correlations can still be very large even after standardizing.  If this is a problem with many datasets and models, I wonder if a version using multiple precision arithmetic might eventually become necessary?

Jim
